learner_visual_status.note: Two source-verified public-domain Jim Conrad Uvalde exact-species photos staged for automated install; matched mm-ruler leaflet and sepal-tubercle macros still needed.

look_here_first: Find the underground BULB and basal trifoliolate leaves: the flowering scapes are separate, LEAFLESS stalks. Compare the broad, deeply notched leaflets (usually 14–34 mm, notch reaching 1/4–4/5 leaflet length) and ABSENCE of oxalate lines by the notch with the smaller, shallowly notched O. violacea. Inspect orange sepal-tip tubercles with a hand lens.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Accepted taxon native to central/southern Texas and northern Mexico at state/regional level (POWO/WFO). Three target-zone native county records not independently certified in this curation pass; do not assign PASS.

morphology_keys.habit: Stemless bulbous perennial; solitary bulb; leaves basal, flowering stalks (scapes) separate and leafless.
morphology_keys.leaves: Three basal leaflets, obtriangular to obcordate, (6–)14–34 mm, notched 1/4–4/5 of length; oxalate lines near notch absent; blades usually glabrous.
morphology_keys.flowers: Scapes generally 11–23 cm; cymes 3–10-flowered; petals white/greenish near base and pink/violet distally, (8–)15–23 mm; 5 sepals with usually 2 orange apical tubercles.
morphology_keys.fruit: Hairy cylindrical capsules 4–12 mm; inspect mature capsules rather than color alone.

comparisons.key_distinctions: O. violacea has generally smaller 8–15 mm leaflets with shallower 1/4–1/3 notch and oxalate lines along notch margins. Yellow woodsorrels have leafy aerial stems instead of basal leaves and separate leafless scapes. Leaflet size overlaps; compare matched notches and sepal tubercles.
comparisons.cautions: Flower color, size and leaf notching overlap. Check oxalate lines at same scale and whether leaves emerge from a bulb. Do not certify county nativity from cultivated specimens.
